title: The Internet: HTTP & HTML

best.what: browser asks a server: GET /login returns HTML, a form sends a POST, the server replies + a cookie = its ID card for you

why: The single best 'what is a backend' video for this course: GET and POST are literally doGet/doPost, and the cookie bit explains how a server remembers you. 7 min, teen level, made for classrooms.

title: The Internet: IP Addresses & DNS

best.what: every device has an address; visiting a site = your computer asking another computer
DNS: names -> addresses, acted out as a phone-around skit

why: Explains what a URL actually points to (their /exec link is a real address on a real server). The DNS skit is short enough to play in class.

title: What is the Internet?

best.what: kids guess what the internet is, then Vint Cerf: messages cut into blocks, sent every direction
who is in charge? nobody / everybody: a network of independent networks

why: 3.7-min hook for the series; the street interviews are funny for 14-year-olds. Opener, not content.

title: The Internet: Packets, Routing & Reliability

best.what: space shuttle on a fleet of trucks = a big file split into packets
TCP as signed delivery: missing packets get resent

why: Good analogies, one level below what they need; library page 'how does data travel'.

title: The Internet: Wires, Cables & Wifi

best.what: bandwidth vs latency: how much per second vs how long one trip takes

why: Mostly physics of bits; the latency minute is the one useful link to 'why does my Apps Script call take a second'.

title: The Internet: How Search Works

best.what: spider crawls ahead of time into a search index so answers are instant

why: The index-built-in-advance idea maps to 'precompute into a Sheet tab instead of scanning every row'; nice optional page.

title: The Internet: Encryption & Public Keys

best.what: Caesar cipher, keys, why brute force works on short keys
public/private key as a mailbox with a deposit slot

why: Well made and teen-friendly, but security is not the course (Ben: no cyber). Keep only as an optional curiosity page.

title: The Internet: Cybersecurity & Crime
why: Digital-citizenship content; nothing they build in this course touches it and Ben ruled out cyber topics.
